newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-ATHERTON VOWS TO PUT THINGS RIGHT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ATHERTON VOWS TO PUT THINGS RIGHT.

text.p: Beleaguered England cricket captain Mike Atherton has vowed to "put things right".

Speaking after the 131 run one-day thrashing by Zimbabwe on Friday, Atherton said: "There's no point crying over spilled milk. You've got two options -- you can either give up or carry on. There's no point in giving up and we'll try our best to put things right".

"I was appointed captain for the winter tour and that doesn't end here (in Zimbabwe), it continues to New Zealand. Perhaps at the end I'll have to reassess but right now I'm looking forward to New Zealand.".
Coach David Lloyd also put a brave face on England's miserable showing in Zimbabwe.
"We will not be down, we will look to go forward. We have
learned some important lessons from Zimbabwe and we will be changing our strategy accordingly in one-day cricket."
Both Lloyd and Atherton reiterated their belief that
England had played some good cricket on tour.
Said Atherton: "I believe we were the better team in the test series. Zimbabwe are a good one-day side -- they field well and bat all the way down and we must give them credit where credit's due."
But in London a Conservative MP was so much at odds with Atherton's view of the tour that he suggested the team should be brought home in disgrace.

Terry Dicks said he was ashamed of the England team. "I think the tour should be abandoned now. They should not be allowed to go out to the sun in New Zealand . They should be brought home in disgrace."

Zimbabwe's bowling hero Eddo Brandes refused to crow over England's defeat. "It's not fair to say that we routed England," he said. "You have good days and bad days. Today things went our way and we caught our catches.

"We are the minnows of world cricket and because of that every game we play is a big one. But we are starting to develop as a side and I'd like to think that we aren't seen as someone to roll over anymore. To beat Zimbabwe today you have to play properly."
Brandes said his hat-trick was only the second of his career and completed a memorable few days after the birth of his second child.

"The first two wickets were a bit lucky -- Nick Knight edged a bad ball and John Crawley missed a straight one -- but I got Nasser Hussain with a real jaffa. He had to play, it moved just enough and Andy Flower took a great catch.
